data.problem: In a class of 60 students, 35 play cricket, 30 play football and 15 play both. How many play at least one of the two, and how many play neither?

options: Because it double counts the 15 who play both
Because the class has only 60 students
steps.why: The 15 who play both are counted once in the 35 and again in the 30. The class size being 60 is a consequence of the error, not the reason for it.
35 + 30 − 15 = 50 students play at least one of the two games.
60 − 50 = 10. Those ten lie outside both circles in the Venn diagram.
35 − 15 = 20. 'Cricket only' always means the total for cricket minus the overlap, and questions often ask for this rather than the total.

data.answer: 50 play at least one game, 10 play neither, and 20 play cricket only.

trick: Every function is a relation, but a relation is a function only if each input has exactly one output. Test it by the vertical line rule: if a vertical line ever cuts the graph twice, it is not a function.

items.why: A function is a relation with the extra condition that each element of the domain maps to exactly one element of the codomain.
A relation may send one input to several outputs, which a function may never do.

items.statement: If A has m elements and B has n, then A × B has mn elements.
items.why: Each of the m first elements pairs with each of the n second ones, so the number of ordered pairs is the product.

items.statement: The domain of f(x) = 1/(x − 2) includes x = 2.
items.why: At x = 2 the denominator is zero, so the function is undefined there. The domain is every real number except 2.

items.statement: A relation on a set with n elements has at most 2^(n²) possibilities.
items.why: A relation is any subset of A × A, which has n² elements, and a set of n² elements has 2^(n²) subsets.
